title: Dusk compact release cheatsheet — Palimpsest roll & traffic fallback (sketch)
content:
Purpose: A compact low-noise quick-reference for a small-batch dusk (post-business-hours) release cadence. Mixes preflight checklist, a 48-hour compact rollout calendar, abbreviated rollback matrix, and a first-pass release notes draft for product/ops review. Intended for the on-call and release shepherd during the watch window.

Context and constraints:
- Target: minor feature bundle + routing tweak to prefer quantized variant on dedicated pools.
- Risk: medium — model routing + autoscaler changes; possible cold-cache spike visible as short tail-latency increase.
- Window: 20:00–02:00 PT (dusk). Use narrow audience slices, strict telemetry gates.
- Targets: hosted API + dedicated capacity (private deployments unaffected).

Contacts (on-call):
- Release lead: Maya Chen
- SRE escalation: Oliver Hart
- Model-serving: Samira Patel
- Telemetry/console: Diego Alvarez
- Product PR: Priya Nair (notify at canary success)

Preflight (T-48h -> T-2h):
- Verify build: tag release/palimpsest/v2026-11-1 at artifact store and checksum.
- Staging smoke: full smoke pass required; attach smoke log to PR.
- Canary plan: routing rules uploaded and referenced in PR; list excluded customer IDs.
- Autoscaler change: headroom bump + capped burst reviewed and documented.
- Observability: token-latency sampling enabled; debug logs gated behind flag.
- Snapshot: save current k8s manifests, routing config, and canary traffic rules.
- Rollback artifact: push previous tag to artifactory and note rollback commands.
- Slack: create #release-palimpsest-watch and update pager matrix.

Immediate pre-window (T-2h -> T-15m):
- Execute smoke runbook and confirm green.
- Notify core teams in watch channel.
- Freeze merges to main for window.
- Start 1% canary for 15m via deployment tool.
- Verify signs stable: errors, 95/99p latency, CPU/GPU, queue depth.
- Abort if any mandatory gate fails.

Compact dusk rollout calendar (steps with wait windows):
1) 20:00 — 1% canary (15m). Monitor short-window signals.
2) 20:15 — if green -> 5% (30m). Hold if marginal; consider narrow variant.
3) 20:45 — 5% -> 20% (45m) if stable.
4) 21:30 — 20% -> 50% (60m) only when rolling averages good.
5) 22:30 — 50% -> 100% (observe first 30m closely).
6) 23:15 — stabilization watch for 2 hours; reduce alert dampening after first clean hour.

Operational gates (quick thresholds):
- Error rate: >0.5% absolute increase in 15m -> gate fail.
- 95th latency: >30% increase sustained for 10m -> gate fail.
- Queue depth: sustained growth 5m with rising CPU/GPU -> hold.
- GPU OOMs/kernel failures: immediate full rollback.
- Cost spike: >2x token-cost projection for 30m -> alert product; consider pause.

Rollback quick matrix:
- Soft abort: stop progression and investigate.
- Partial rollback: revert to previous stable percentage when trend persists >30m.
- Full rollback: redeploy previous tag and restore routing config if critical gates trip. Target restore 10–20 min.
- After rollback: collect dumps, logs, create postmortem stub within 24h, notify stakeholders.

Post-roll smoke checklist (validation):
- Embeddings sanity: generate samples and check distribution norms.
- Chat regression: 50 scripted prompts; compare top-k token diffs.
- Streaming: validate session flushing under 120s.
- Customer routes: spot-check top 5 internal customers for errors.

Console/telemetry tasks:
- Create ephemeral dashboard palimpsest-dusk-watch: panels for error-rate, p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU, queue depth, cost-per-token.
- Add temporary alert rules scoped to rollout with adjusted thresholds.
- Enable debug traces for model-routing for first 30m after each percentage increase.

Release notes (draft for product review):
Title: Palimpsest rollout — routing prioritization + autoscaler tuning
Summary: Prioritize quantized variants on dedicated pools and tune autoscaler headroom to reduce tail latency for embeddings and small chat workloads. Expected: improved p95/p99 latency and better burst handling on dedicated pools.
Changes:
- Routing: prefer quantized model variants on dedicated GPUs for latency-sensitive tiers.
- Autoscaler: adjusted scale-up thresholds and added capped burst capacity to reduce cold-start latency.
- Telemetry: increased token-level latency sampling for the initial minute of sessions.
Known issues:
- Cold-cache spike possible first 30 minutes; mitigation: limited rate-limiting and pre-warm script on dedicated pools.
- Edge-case: slight uptick in errors for very long contexts; canary gating and rollback prepared.
Rollout plan: progressive 1→5→20→50→100% over dusk window with strict telemetry gates.
Contacts: Maya Chen (release lead), Priya Nair (product).

Open items / TODOs:
- Confirm pre-warm frequency and exact excluded customer IDs (Priya).
- Finalize alert damping with SRE (Oliver).
- Document how to revert autoscaler config only (without routing change).

Watch tips:
- Keep Slack posts terse — raw metrics at percentage milestones only.
- If canary unstable but not failing gates, give 15m trend window before escalations.
- Snapshot dashboards as JSON for postmortem reproducibility.

Postmortem stub: create if any gate fails; capture timeline, decision points, logs, traces, rollback steps, and action items within 48h.

Quick commands:
- deploy: ./tools/deploy --tag release/palimpsest/v2026-11-1 --env prod --route palimpsest-canary
- rollback: ./tools/rollback --tag release/palimpsest/previous --route restore
- observe: ./tools/observe --dashboard palimpsest-dusk-watch

End of sketch. Expand to full runbook only if issues occur during the window.
